case_title: Ramesh Chilwal v. State of Uttarakhand
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.213; Gangsters Act s.213; Arms Act s.27
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC, s.213 Gangsters Act, s.27 Arms Act; life imprisonment and fine; 10 years and fine; 7 years and fine
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 IPC, violation of s.213 Gangsters Act, violation of s.27 Arms Act
neutral_facts: The accused was involved in a case where the victim was killed. The accused was convicted of murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code. The accused was also found guilty of violating Section 213 of the Gangsters Act and Section 27 of the Arms Act. The trial court sentenced the accused to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,00,000, with additional terms for defaulting on the fine. The accused was also sentenced to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 50,000 for the Gangsters Act violation, and 7 years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 25,000 for the Arms Act violation. The sentences were confirmed by the High Court, and the Supreme Court clarified that all sentences would run concurrently.
